status: REFUTED - by a declared product invariant, before any measurement
implemented: 34 insertions across 2 product files: PackLane::seals_every_record() in pack/layout.rs, and in pack/placement.rs::select_many a lane that seals per record stops consulting append_fits and closes its pack after placing.

refuting_evidence.assertion: assert_eq!(outcome.packs_created, 1, "both objects share one pack") and assert_eq!(counters.packs_read, 1)
refuting_evidence.observed: packs_created = 2, packs_read would be 2 - the two 60,000-byte whole-file objects each got their own pack
refuting_evidence.command: cargo +1.85.1 test --locked --manifest-path core/Cargo.toml -p layerfs-storage  (12 passed, 1 FAILED)
refuting_evidence.full_suite_state: only cas_reuse::one_operation_can_save_two_files_into_shared_packs failed; the other 12 cas_reuse cases and every earlier-compiled target passed

why_this_is_a_refutation_and_not_an_obst: The test does not measure a preference; it declares a product property: two whole-file objects saved in one operation SHARE a pack, and reading both reads ONE pack. Pack sharing is the read-amplification contract - a pack is a read unit, so objects are deliberately co-located. PR-A1 traded that declared read property for write bytes, which is a change of contract, not an optimisation. The test was not modified and the change was reverted in full (git checkout); cas_reuse is 13/13 green on the reverted tree.

consequence.statement: Pack sharing is load-bearing, so the WholeFile and PooledMetadata lanes MUST append to a shared pack. Appending is what rewrites the whole body, because the directory grows and moves every body behind it (cas/placement.rs:203-205), which pack/layout.rs::directory_is_starts_only() makes true for WholeFile alone.
consequence.therefore: The 7.5917x amplification is INHERENT TO THE CURRENT PACK FORMAT. It cannot be removed by any placement or lifetime rule without either breaking a declared read property (PR-A1, refuted here) or changing the format.

routes_that_remain: PR-C1 (Squad C): batch placements so fewer writes happen while packs stay shared. Format-neutral. NOT refuted. Costs a step-boundary change whose code-level blockers are recorded in preregistration-PR-A1.json: availability.inserted and sealed_rows must move to queue time or the duplicate-offer hazard they exist to prevent returns; every owner read must flush first (multi_writer.rs:31 reads its own private objects mid-save); finish_inner must flush first; and a batch bound is required, where the only existing candidates (capacities.transaction_rows = 8191, batch_objects = 512) hold the arbitration lock far longer than today's one group.

Owner ruling on a Store-format change: a directory-last pack layout, or reserved directory space, would make an append write only the new bytes and remove the amplification at its root. This campaign does not propose a format and did not implement one.
what_was_NOT_run: No harness benchmark row was produced for PR-A1. The treatment was refuted at the test gate, which the pre-registration listed as a refutation criterion; measuring a treatment known to break a declared invariant would have been waste, and the reference row is unchanged. This is recorded as NOT_RUN with that reason rather than as a missing measurement.
